summary: Spike of credential-stuffing attempts followed by enrichment-API-driven privileged-invite creations
description:
Issue summary: On 2026-03-12 09:12 UTC we observed a large automated login attempt spike against the Redwood identity endpoints originating from a small set of IP subnets. Around the same time, a cluster of privileged invite tokens were created via the internal /admin/invite API. Impact: potential unauthorized creation of privileged invites and risk of lateral access. No confirmed end-user breaches yet; invites were invalidated as a precaution. Environment: prod (us-east-1).

High-level timeline: 2026-03-12 08:58 UTC - first credential-stuffing alerts from auth-rate-limit; 09:05 UTC - enrichment API calls to breached-password vendor spike; 09:10 UTC - spike in POST /admin/invite creating admin-level invites; 09:15 UTC - automated remediation started (invite invalidation, key rotation).

Why this is concerning: attack pattern suggests automated credential stuffing combined with use of our enrichment/verification pipeline which had a service integration able to escalate or create invites via a synchronous job. The enrichment calls appear to have been used as part of a scripted flow to verify account existence and then trigger invite creation from a service account.

Initial mitigation applied: blocked 10 suspicious IP ranges via WAF; rotated the service account credentials used by enrichment pipeline; invalidated all outstanding admin invites created between 09:00-09:20 UTC; enabled stricter rate limits on /admin endpoints pending permanent fix.

Requested priority: urgent security follow-up and forensic preservation of logs and artifacts.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate high-volume login attempts against auth.v1/login with common username lists under rate-limit thresholds to reproduce detection alerts
Trigger enrichment flow by making enrichment API calls for enumerated emails and observe whether invite creation job is invoked when enrichment returns 'known' status
Attempt repeat POST /admin/invite calls from a service token with similar call pattern to verify server-side rate-limiting behavior
observed_evidence: Auth logs: ~37k failed login attempts over 12 minutes from 18 IPs clustered in two ASNs (timestamps 2026-03-12T08:58:00Z - 2026-03-12T09:10:00Z)
Enrichment vendor API: 1.2k enrichment requests for 'breach-check' returned positive for ~420 accounts (calls share X-Request-ID header series)
API gateway logs: 23 POST /admin/invite calls from service account token svc-enrich-01 between 2026-03-12T09:09:40Z and 2026-03-12T09:11:05Z (userAgent bot/1.2)

Created invite tokens: 18 admin-level invites created; 5 subsequently accepted (internal test accounts) before invalidation; we believe acceptance attempts were automated and against staging-like accounts
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: credential-stuffing enumeration identified valid accounts; attacker script called enrichment endpoint which returned 'known' and triggered downstream invite creation via a legacy synchronous job path

Hypothesis 2: service account svc-enrich-01 had overly broad privileges allowing it to call invite-creation as part of a data-enrichment workflow; attacker abuse of compromised CI/automation credentials cannot be ruled out
Evidence shows service token present in X-Forwarded-Auth header on invite calls; token rotation and audit confirms token was active at time of calls

SRE traced the invite-create code path and found an unthrottled async worker (invite-provisioner) that processed enrichment results and called the admin-invite API; this worker lacked request-level RBAC enforcement

No indications yet of lateral movement beyond invite creation; logs of subsequent invites show immediate invalidation at 09:16 UTC; however, forensic snapshots of Kafka topic 'enrichment-results' were saved for retention
comments: 2026-03-12 09:22 UTC - Marcus Lee (SRE): initial triage complete. Confirmed spike and invite creations. Rotated svc-enrich-01 and blacklisted IP ranges in WAF. Saved Kafka snapshots and auth logs to /forensics/incidents/INT-999550.

2026-03-12 10:05 UTC - Priya Nair (SecOps): running full token sweep for automation accounts used by enrichment pipeline; creating JIRA tasks for privilege scoping review. Asked Product to review whether invite creation should be reachable from enrichment worker.

2026-03-12 11:30 UTC - Tom Reynolds (Identity): found invite-provisioner worker had no RBAC check; opened PR to gate invite creation behind explicit role check (see PR #4251). Added immediate rate limiting on worker queue.

2026-03-12 14:00 UTC - Aisha Kapoor (Reporter): confirmed invalidation of outstanding invites and rotation completed. Requesting SecOps postmortem and a list of any accounts that accepted invites during incident window.
2026-03-13 09:00 UTC - Priya Nair (SecOps): follow-up: 3 internal test accounts accepted invites; audit shows no external accounts accepted. Preparing preliminary postmortem for 2026-03-14.

2026-03-13 16:45 UTC - Marcus Lee (SRE): WAF rule and rate-limit measures deployed to prod permanently. Monitoring for repeat patterns; set alert for >100 enrichment calls / min from single token or IP range.
resolution: Temporary: rotated the svc-enrich-01 service token, invalidated all admin invites created in the window, blocked offending IP ranges at WAF, captured forensic logs. Permanent: applied RBAC checks to invite-provisioner (PR merged), added request-level authorization and rate-limits, scheduled an identity team audit to remove invite creation from enrichment worker and instead surface candidates to a human-approved queue. Follow-up tasks created for Product and SecOps to review enrichment privileges and vendor usage policy.
next_steps: Complete SecOps postmortem and circulate to Exec and IR teams (owner: Priya Nair)
Product to design UX change to require human approval for any admin-level invites created by automated workflows (owner: Tom Reynolds)
Run account compromise sweep for any accounts with enrichment-positive flags in the 24h window (owner: SRE)
Add additional alerting rules to detect enrichment->invite call chains and throttle automatically (owner: SRE)
Engage vendor to rate-limit enrichment API responses per account and review contractual abuse detection (owner: VendorOps)
Prepare customer-facing note if any external account evidence emerges (owner: CS)
Close ticket after 7-day monitoring window with no recurrence
